question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Have your heart in your mouth

options.text: Accusing someone of faults which you have

solution:
The correct answer is **"Feeling extremely nervous."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The expression **"have your heart in your mouth"** is an idiomatic phrase that describes a state of intense anxiety, nervousness, or anticipation. (तीव्र चिंता, घबराहट या प्रत्याशा की स्थिति)

 
 
• **Example**: *As the suspenseful thriller reached its climax, the audience had their hearts in their mouths, eagerly awaiting the unexpected twist.*
 
 
 
• 
 
The meaning of the idiom **"have your heart in your mouth"** is **"feeling extremely nervous."**

 
 
• 
 
Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.
